the.definition: Used to refer to a specific person or thing.
examples: The book on the table is mine.

be.definition: To exist or have a specific quality or state.
examples: I want to be a doctor.

to.definition: Used to indicate direction, purpose, or relation.
examples: I need to finish this work.

of.definition: Used to show possession, origin, or relation.
examples: The color of the sky is blue.

and.definition: Used to connect words, phrases, or clauses.
examples: Bread and butter are on the table.

a.definition: Used before singular nouns to mean one or any.
examples: I saw a bird in the garden.
The keys are in my bag.

that.definition: Used to point to a specific thing or introduce a clause.
examples: I believe that he is right.

have.definition: To possess, hold, or experience something.
examples: We have lunch at noon every day.

i.definition: The speaker or writer referring to themselves.

it.definition: Used to refer to a thing, animal, or situation.
examples: I bought a laptop and it works well.

for.definition: Intended to benefit or because of someone or something.
examples: She studied hard for the exam.

not.definition: Used to make a word or statement negative.
examples: He did not answer the question.

on.definition: Physically in contact with and supported by a surface.
examples: The book is on the desk.
She put her coat on the chair.

with.definition: In company of or having something.
examples: She went to the cinema with her friends.
Coffee with milk is my favorite.

he.definition: Used to refer to a male person or animal.

as.definition: Used to compare or indicate role or time.
examples: As I was leaving, it started to rain.

you.definition: Used to refer to the person being addressed.
examples: Can you help me with this?

do.definition: To perform an action or activity.
examples: What do you do on weekends?
I do my homework after school.

at.definition: Used to show a point in space or time.
examples: We meet at the café at 3 p.m.

this.definition: Used to identify something close to the speaker.

but.definition: Used to introduce an idea that contrasts with the previous one.
examples: She is small but very strong.
I wanted to go, but I was busy.

his.definition: Belonging to or associated with a male person.
examples: His phone is on the table.

by.definition: Near, through, or during the action of someone.
examples: The novel was written by a famous author.

from.definition: Indicating the point in space or time at which something starts.
examples: The shop is open from 9 to 5.

they.definition: Used to refer to two or more people or things.

we.definition: Used by a speaker to refer to themselves and others.
examples: We are going to the beach tomorrow.
We need more time to finish.

say.definition: To utter words in order to express thoughts or information.
examples: He said he would be late.

her.definition: Used as the object of a verb or to show possession for a female.

she.definition: Used to refer to a female person or animal.

examples: You can call or text me.

an.definition: The form of a used before words beginning with a vowel sound.

will.definition: Used to express future tense or willingness.
examples: Will you join us for dinner?

my.definition: Belonging to or associated with the speaker.
examples: My parents live in the countryside.
This is my first time here.

one.definition: The number 1; a single person or thing.
examples: One of the windows is broken.

all.definition: The whole quantity or extent of something.

would.definition: Used to express conditional mood or polite requests.
examples: I would like a glass of water.
What would you do in that situation?

there.definition: In, at, or to that place or position.
examples: There is a park near my house.

their.definition: Belonging to or associated with people or things previously mentioned.

what.definition: Used to ask for information about something.
examples: What time does the meeting start?

so.definition: To such a great extent; therefore.
examples: She was so tired that she fell asleep.
I was hungry, so I ate a sandwich.

up.definition: Toward a higher place or position.

out.definition: Away from the inside or center.
examples: He went out for a walk.

if.definition: On the condition that; supposing that.
examples: If it rains, we will stay home.
Call me if you need help.

who.definition: Used to ask or talk about which person.

get.definition: To obtain, receive, or become something.
examples: I need to get some milk.
She got a new job last month.

which.definition: Used to ask or talk about one or more possibilities.
examples: This is the book which I recommended.

go.definition: To move or travel from one place to another.
examples: She goes to work by bus.

me.definition: Used as the object when the speaker is involved.
examples: She gave me a beautiful gift.

when.definition: At the time that something happens.
examples: When I arrived, everyone was waiting.
Call me when you are ready.

make.definition: To create, produce, or cause something to happen.

can.definition: To be able to; to have permission to.

like.definition: To enjoy or find pleasant; similar to.

time.definition: The continuous passage of existence; a particular moment.
examples: We don't have much time left.

no.definition: Used to give a negative response.
examples: There is no milk in the fridge.

him.definition: Used as the object form of he.
examples: I saw him at the library.

know.definition: To have information or understanding about something.
examples: Do you know where she lives?

take.definition: To get hold of something; to carry or accept.
examples: It takes about an hour to get there.

people.definition: Human beings in general or a group of persons.
examples: People from many countries live here.

into.definition: Moving to the inside of something.
examples: Pour the water into the glass.
This year has been very busy.

your.definition: Belonging to the person being addressed.

good.definition: Of high quality or morally right.

examples: Some people prefer tea over coffee.

could.definition: Used to indicate possibility or polite request.

them.definition: Used as the object form of they.
examples: I invited them to the party.
Give them some time to think.

see.definition: To perceive with the eyes; to understand.
examples: I can see the mountains from here.

other.definition: Different from the one already mentioned.
examples: Do you have any other questions?
She is taller than her brother.

then.definition: At that time; next in order.
examples: We had dinner, then watched a movie.
If you're ready, then let's start.
Now is the time to act.

look.definition: To direct your eyes toward something; to appear.

examples: She is the only child in her family.

come.definition: To move toward or arrive at a place.

its.definition: Belonging to or associated with a thing or animal.

over.definition: Above or across something; more than.
examples: The plane flew over the city.
She is over twenty years old.

think.definition: To use the mind to form ideas or opinions.
examples: I think this plan will work.
She speaks French and also German.
I also want to join the trip.

back.definition: To or toward the rear; returning to a previous state.

examples: We went for a walk after dinner.

use.definition: To employ something for a purpose.
examples: I use my laptop for work.
How do you spell your name?

our.definition: Belonging to the speaker and others.

work.definition: To do a job or task; to function properly.

first.definition: Coming before all others in time or order.
examples: This is my first visit to Japan.

well.definition: In a good way; in good health.
examples: I hope you feel well soon.
This is the best way to learn.
Is this the way to the station?

even.definition: Used to emphasize something surprising or extreme.
examples: Even children can use this app.

new.definition: Not existing before; recently made or discovered.
examples: We moved to a new apartment.

want.definition: To desire or wish for something.

examples: I stayed home because I was sick.
Because it was late, we left early.

any.definition: One or some of a thing, no matter which.

these.definition: Used to refer to things near the speaker.

give.definition: To hand over or provide something to someone.
examples: She gave him a warm smile.
We spent the whole day at the beach.

most.definition: The greatest amount or to the greatest degree.
examples: She is the most talented singer here.

us.definition: Used as the object form of we.
examples: Can you help us with this project?

forest.definition: A large area covered chiefly with trees and undergrowth.
examples: We walked through the forest for hours.
Many animals live in the forest.

happy.definition: Feeling or showing pleasure and contentment.
examples: She was happy to see her friends.

learn.definition: To gain knowledge or skill through study or experience.
examples: I want to learn how to cook.

school.definition: A place where children go to be educated.
examples: She walks to school every day.
Our school has a large library.

water.definition: A clear liquid essential for life.
examples: The water in the lake is clean.

friend.definition: A person you know well and like.
examples: We met an old friend at the café.

world.definition: The earth and all the people and things on it.
examples: Travel helps you see the world.
The whole world watched the event.
